title: Stage fright at the Paris concerts
summary: He was terrified to play Caravan at the first Paris concert but, after a brandy, played it well at the second.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well, I don't know anything about that. I know we went to -- it we started in with Paris, I think it was; yes, we had two concerts in Paris.
Yes, because your cousin was in Paris.
We played a concert in Paris, which I

mean, I was just scared to death, you know, because that particular night, we had two concerts. The first concert, the place was jam packed with people in tuxedoes and all this, oh, it was a terrific thing.

And Duke was calling for in the program, I saw the program, where Caravan was the second or third number on the program. So I passed Willie over there and I said, 'Tell him don't play Caravan now, because I am a little nervous, and to leave it for later on'. So he didn't pay no attention, you know?

That's one thing about Duke you could count on -- he said to me, 'Don't worry about nothing. I'm behind you, I'm behind you.' So he was and he announced that I was the composer -- 'Caravan will be played now by Juan Tizol'. You know, I couldn't even get up to the mike? I couldn't even get up to the mike at the front of the stage; I got up and my stomach was going like, I don't know like what; I ended up playing the melody, which I thought I could play, but I was scared to death and shaking. I was, almost sick.

The next concert, to steady myself I went to the bar and got myself some brandy to fix me up and I went over there, and I saw the program was the same way, because it was different people. So like I said, I got this brandy and I drank it -- it was a small bottle anyhow, and I took that and got myself together, and I told Duke, 'I'm going

out there tonight; I'm going out there and I'm going to play 'Pyramid' Caravan or Perdido -- I'll play anything!" So I went over there and did my job, and even my cousin that was over there in Paris then, he was on the top floor with his girlfriend, and he said he noticed that I on the first one, was nervous or something. Well, anyhow, the second time, I played "Caravan," and everything was all right; I got up and took my bow, and acted just like a soldier, you know? I saluted and did everything, you know? I was wonderful then.
But why were you so scared? You had been appearing in front of audiences for years.
Yeah, but you'd be surprised -- in that particular concert, see, the people were expecting Duke Ellington for a long, long time.
